packageRules.description: Bumps of the binary, the images and the stack ship to users, so they release. Anything new lands here too, which is the safer default: it shows up rather than passing unseen.
Except the pipeline, which no user ever runs.
Go modules are reviewed as one batch, so the split into minor and patch is lifted for them.
Bundle the digest refreshes that ship, which carry no version to review.
The same for the pipeline, kept apart so each group carries one commit type.
A digest names a build, not a release, so it has no date an age check could measure.
A minor is compatible by the rules, but a new minor of a base image or the toolchain can still change behaviour.
Images tracking a rolling tag do not need a digest pin.
Label major updates so they get a deliberate review.
Renovate updates itself through the renovate-version line, which the github-actions manager reads as an image but which takes no digest. It also deserves a read of its notes.
